Currently
column2: most files in the tracefs directory test if tracing_disabled is

column1: set. If so
column2: it should return -ENODEV. The tracing_disabled is called when

column1: tracing is found to be broken. Originally it was done in case the ring
buffer was found to be corrupted
column2: and we wanted to prevent reading it from

column1: crashing the kernel. But it's also called if a tracing selftest fails on
boot. It's a one way switch. That is
disabled until reboot.
As most tracefs files can also be used by instances in the tracefs
directory
column2: they need to be carefully done. Each instance has a trace_array

column1: associated to it
column2: and when the instance is removed

column1: freed. But if an instance is opened with a reference to the trace_array
then it requires looking up the trace_array to get its ref counter (as there
could be a race with it being deleted and the open itself). Once it is
found
column2: a reference is added to prevent the instance from being removed (and

column1: the trace_array associated with it freed).
Combine the two checks (tracing_disabled and trace_array_get()) into a
single helper function. This will also make it easier to add lockdown to
tracefs later.
